o: Heavenly Father, thank You for allowing a new day to dawn. Before I go to my occupations, I want to pause before You and acknowledge that everything good comes from Your hand. You care for the earth, You send the rain and You make fruit grow in its season. Take care also of my life, my home and my steps throughout this day.

Lord, today I want to be good soil for Your Word. Remove from my heart the stones of hardness, the thorns of anxiety and everything that keeps Your truth from taking deep root. Give me an attentive ear to listen to You and a heart willing to obey what You show me, even if I do not understand everything at this moment.

Help me sow kind words, gestures of patience and works of goodness wherever I find myself. May I not be discouraged if I do not see results quickly, for I know that it is You who give the growth. Bless my family, my neighbors and those who need a word of encouragement today. Guide me by Your Spirit and sustain me by Your peace. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: Jesus was beside the Sea of Galilee and the crowd was so great that he had to get into a boat to teach, while the people stood on the shore. There, with simple words, he told a story everyone could understand, for everyone knew the work of the fields: the parable of the sower.

He said that a sower went out to sow. As he scattered the seed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it. Other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was little soil; it sprang up at once, but when the sun rose it was scorched, because it had no root. Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it. But other seed fell on good soil and produced fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

The disciples were left pondering, then asked him what it meant. Jesus explained to them that the seed is the word of the kingdom. The path represents the heart that hears but does not understand, and the enemy takes away what was sown. The rocky ground is the one who receives the word with joy, but without root, and who stumbles when difficulty comes. The thorns are the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches. The good soil is the one who hears the word, understands it and bears fruit.

The most beautiful thing in this story is that the sower does not lose heart. He keeps casting the seed generously, knowing that some will be lost, but that another part will yield a great harvest. This is how God is with us: he does not stop speaking to us, he does not stop sowing, and he waits for our heart to open so that it may bear fruit.
m.c: May the Lord go with you from the first hour of this day and remind you that in his hands everything grows in its time. Walk without fear, with an open heart and your trust placed in the one who cares for you. May his peace be your strength until evening.
m: The parable of the sower reminds us that the fruit of our life depends not only on effort, but on the condition of the heart that receives the Word of God. The seed is the same for everyone; what changes is the soil. That is why today's question is not how much we know, but how willing we are to receive and to obey.

Think for a moment of your heart as a field. Perhaps in some areas it is hard like the path, because you have heard the same truth many times and it no longer touches you. Perhaps elsewhere there are stones: you are enthusiastic at first, but you give up when difficulties come. Or perhaps there are thorns, those worries and rushes that leave no room for what is important. God does not condemn you for this; he invites you to prepare the soil.

Today you can take very concrete steps. Begin by calmly reading a passage of the Bible and ask yourself what God is asking of you. Write down one thing and decide to do it before the day ends. If you feel that worry is choking you, breathe, pray and give that burden to the Lord before continuing your tasks. Pulling up a thorn in time is better than letting it grow.

And remember that you are also a sower. Every kind word, every quiet help and every example of patience is a seed. You will not always see the harvest, and that is fine. The psalmist says that God visits the earth, waters it and blesses its sprouting growth. Sow today with hope, trusting that the Lord will make grow what you have sown with love.

o: Lord Jesus, at the end of this day, I come to You with a grateful heart. Thank You for every moment of the day, for the work accomplished, for the bread of the table and for the people You placed on my path. Even in the difficult moments, Your hand was with me and You did not let me walk alone.

I now give You what worried me today and what I left unfinished. You know my weariness, my doubts and the thoughts that will not leave me in peace. I want to leave them at Your feet, like a child resting in his father's arms. Teach me to trust without so many questions and to receive Your kingdom with simplicity.

Watch tonight over my family and all those I love. Bless the children, the sick, the elderly and those who feel alone. Give rest to those who suffer and peace to those who cannot sleep. May I wake tomorrow with new strength, knowing that my life is safe in Your hands. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: One day, on the road to Judea, people were bringing children to Jesus so that he might touch and bless them. They were mothers and fathers who knew that this Master was different from the others. But the disciples, thinking Jesus was too busy to attend to little ones, rebuked them and tried to turn them away.

When Jesus saw it, he was indignant with his disciples and said to them: “Let the little children come to me; do not hinder them, for to such belongs the kingdom of God.” These words must have surprised everyone. In that time, children had no place of importance in adult conversations, but for Jesus, they were the closest to his kingdom.

Then he added something that changed the way faith is understood: “Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it.” A child does not come to his father with a résumé or a list of merits. He comes with open hands, with trust, knowing he will be welcomed. This is how Jesus wants us to come to him.

And the account ends with a very tender image: Jesus took the children in his arms, laid his hands on them and blessed them. It was not a hurried gesture. He stopped, embraced them and prayed for each one of them. Today, at the end of the day, that same blessing is open to you. You have nothing to prove; it is enough to draw near, set down your burdens and let yourself be wrapped in the love of God.
t.c: As you close this day, give thanks for what has been lived and place in God's hands everything you could not settle. He keeps watch while you sleep and does not tire of caring for you. Rest in peace, and may his blessing cover you tonight like a quiet embrace.
m: Psalm 62 tells us: “For God alone my soul waits in silence.” This word, rest, is very precious at the end of a day. It is not only about letting the body sleep, but about the soul finding a safe place to stop. And that place, according to the psalmist, is God himself, our rock, our salvation and our refuge.

Very often we arrive at evening with a mind full of unfinished things. We replay conversations, we calculate what is lacking and we worry about what is coming. Jesus, in welcoming the children, shows us another way: that of simple trust. A child in his father's arms does not solve the world's problems, but he rests because he knows someone stronger holds him.

Tonight you can practice this rest in a very concrete way. Take a few minutes before sleeping, turn off the screens and make a short list of the things that worry you. Then pray for each one and give it to the Lord in simple words. If a pending task can wait until tomorrow, leave it there. If there is a person with whom you need to be reconciled, decide to speak to them at dawn.

The psalmist invites us to pour out our hearts before God, for he is our refuge. You do not have to feign strength before him. You can tell him that you are tired, that you are afraid or that you do not understand something. And then you can rest, not because everything is settled, but because God is with you. His love sustains you tonight, as it sustained the children Jesus took in his arms.
